A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same SE-GS study, with matching core methods and benchmarks. v3 includes supplementary material absent from the supplied v1; newly documented details can be compared without assuming they represent newly implemented procedures.

before.justification: v1 reports original SE-GS experiments on four datasets, qualitative renderings, and analyses of model count, training speed, and perturbation strategies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds model-diversity analysis and supplementary perturbation sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: The two-model pipeline, co-pruning, losses, and inference procedure remain. However, Equation 8 changes uncertainty normalization from sqrt(sum)/S to sqrt(sum/S), and Section 4.1 replaces the stated unit-variance perturbations with parameter-scaled Gaussian noise. These are limited revisions to the reported specification; the PDFs do not establish whether implementation or experiments changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate few-shot novel-view synthesis on LLFF, DTU, Mip-NeRF360, and 50 sampled MVImgNet scenes. The benchmark view counts remain unchanged. The added analyses use retained LLFF coverage rather than introducing another domain or task.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 add DNGaussian participation in the 6-view and 9-view comparisons, where v1 reports dashes. Its 3-view participation and the other benchmark comparator memberships remain unchanged. CoR-GS model-count variants and Random/Gradient-Aware perturbation alternatives already appear in v1.

E3.justification: v3 removes AVGE from Tables 1–3 and adds model-agreement PSNR as a diagnostic. New analyses sweep perturbation intervals from 100 to 900 iterations and fixed noise multipliers from 0.01 to 0.3. The stated default noise distribution is revised to adaptive scaling, while benchmark splits, view counts, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained model-count/speed comparison and perturbation-strategy ablation, v3 adds model agreement versus synthesis quality in Figure 7, interval sensitivity in Figure 9, noise-level sensitivity in Figure 10, and the evolution of the perturbed-Gaussian fraction in Figure 11. These substantially expand examination of the central perturbation mechanism.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty on benchmark estimates. The pixel-level uncertainty computation is part of the algorithm, rather than statistical uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: Shared SE-GS PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS values in Tables 1–4 and the Table 5 ablation values remain unchanged. Newly reported DNGaussian PSNRs are 22.01/22.62 on LLFF and 22.56/25.25 on DTU for 6/9 views. Figures 7 and 9–11 substantially expand findings on diversity, perturbation sensitivity, and the perturbed-Gaussian fraction. AVGE entries disappear, and Figure 5 replaces one qualitative example. These are additional or removed results, not same-setting SE-GS performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 8 changes the uncertainty normalization mathematically, moving 1/S inside the square root. The supplement adds explicit definitions of the adaptive threshold in Equation 15 and parameter-dependent noise scale in Equation 16. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains uncertainty-aware self-ensembling for few-shot 3DGS, claimed to mitigate overfitting, outperform competitors across four datasets, avoid additional ground-truth signals, and incur negligible additional overhead. The rewritten abstract, introduction, and conclusion largely retain these claims.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly frames perturbation as a tradeoff between model diversity and supervision reliability. It explains failures with overly frequent, strong, or weak perturbations and identifies unreliable models as a target for future outlier identification. These add concrete qualifications to the existing mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: The new supplement supplies operational details missing from v1: threshold parameters r=0.05 and theta=0.01, Gaussian selection through projected overlap, parameter-scaled noise with a multiplier decaying from 0.08 to 0.02, and specific DTU scans requiring random initialization. The direct repository link becomes a project-page link; v3 also introduces inconsistent released-versus-future-release wording.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on deep ensembles, transformation-consistent self-ensembling, SE-SSD, and Plenoxels, while removing several background references on volume rendering, augmentation, dropout, and left-atrium segmentation. The principal positioning against CoR-GS and other sparse-view reconstruction methods remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries and Motivations become separate subsections, Temporal Samples in 3DGS becomes Uncertainty-Aware Perturbation, and terminology shifts toward perturbed models. A structured supplement expands the explanation of ensemble learning and implementation.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the pipeline and buffer diagrams, adds Figures 7–11, and revises Figure 5 with zoomed details and a box example replacing the watch. Tables 1–3 lose AVGE columns, Table 3 becomes a single-column display, and several figures and tables are relocated. These constitute substantial visual and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: v1 defers essential Gaussian-selection details to supplementary material absent from its PDF and provides limited testing of perturbation settings. v3 supplies operational threshold and noise specifications and targeted diversity, interval, and noise analyses, substantially improving reproducibility and support for the central design. Dropping AVGE and introducing inconsistent code-release wording are narrower drawbacks; the principal benchmark results remain intact.
